# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```

skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md-1----
skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md-2-name: writing-shape
skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md-3-description: "Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph."
skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md:4:disable-model-invocation: true
skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md-5----
skills/in-progress/writing-shape/SKILL.md-6-
.agents/invocation.md-1-# Model-invoked vs user-invoked
.agents/invocation.md-2-
.agents/invocation.md-3-Every `SKILL.md` in this repo is a skill. The one axis that splits them is **invocation**, who can reach it:
.agents/invocation.md-4-
.agents/invocation.md:5:- **User-invoked**: reachable **only by the human typing its name**. Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in the frontmatter (Claude Code) and `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` in `agents/openai.yaml` (Codex). The `description` is **human-facing**: a one-line summary read by a person browsing slash-commands. Strip trigger lists ("Use when the user says…").
.agents/invocation.md:6:- **Model-invoked**: reachable by **model or user**. The default: omit `disable-model-invocation` and the `policy` block from `agents/openai.yaml`. The `description` is **model-facing** and keeps rich trigger phrasing ("Use when the user wants…, mentions…, asks for…") so auto-invocation fires. The test for whether a skill should stay model-invoked: _could the model usefully reach for this autonomously?_ (Reuse is the reason to extract a skill, not the test.)
.agents/invocation.md-7-
.agents/invocation.md-8-Each harness excludes a user-invoked skill from the model's reach in its own way, so nothing but the human can fire it: no other skill can. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but it can never reach another user-invoked skill.
.agents/invocation.md-9-
.agents/invocation.md:10:Every skill also carries an `agents/openai.yaml` beside its `SKILL.md`. It holds Codex UI metadata: `interface.display_name` and `interface.short_description` for the skill picker, and, for user-invoked skills, the `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` that pairs with `disable-model-invocation`. Keep the two in sync: a skill is user-invoked in both harnesses or neither.
.agents/invocation.md-11-
.agents/invocation.md-12-Bucket `README.md`s and the top-level `README.md` group entries into **User-invoked** and **Model-invoked**.

Two levers, and `/skills` is the front-end for one of them.

**1. `skillOverrides` in settings.json** — this is what `/skills` writes. Keyed by skill name, four values:

```json
{
  "skillOverrides": {
    "graphify": "on",                    // default if absent: model can auto-invoke
    "turborepo": "name-only",            // listed to the model without its description
    "scope-check": "user-invocable-only",// hidden from the model, /scope-check still works
    "shadcn": "off"                      // hidden from both
  }
}
```

So "automatic" = `on` (or absent). To make a skill slash-only, set `user-invocable-only`. Works in `~/.claude/settings.json` (user), `.claude/settings.json` (project), or `.claude/settings.local.json`; project wins over user. Your `~/.claude/settings.json` has no `skillOverrides` block yet — that's why `/skills` reported "No changes".

**2. Skill frontmatter** — if you own the skill, `disable-model-invocation: true` in its SKILL.md makes it user-invoked by default (e.g. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/.../writing-shape/SKILL.md:4`). An `off` override can still hide it entirely, but you can't override an author's `disable-model-invocation` back to automatic.

Beyond that: what actually triggers an automatic invocation is the `description` field — Claude matches the task against it, so rich "Use when the user asks…, mentions…" phrasing makes a skill fire more readily, and a terse description makes it fire less. And `disableBundledSkills: true` (or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1`) drops all the Claude Code–shipped skills at once, leaving plugins and `.claude/skills/` alone.
